scenes.title: Exchange-Traded Futures vs OTC Forward Contracts

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Venue & Standardization: Futures trade on public exchanges with standardized sizes; Forwards trade privately with customized bilateral terms [fact-01, fact-02].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Settlement & Credit Risk: Futures use daily mark-to-market clearing house margining; Forwards settle at maturity and carry direct counterparty credit risk [fact-02].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Liquidity & Unwinding: Futures close out via offsetting trades; Forwards are held to maturity or require bilateral consent [fact-02].

scenes.title: Business Snapshot 1.1: Anatomy of Lehman Brothers Bankruptcy

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 1 — 31:1 Extreme Leverage: Exempt from bank capital rules, Lehman operated with a thin 3.23% equity buffer [fact-04, fact-05].

beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 3 — Subprime Exposure & Funding Freeze: Unhedged subprime assets on short-term debt collapsed when lenders stopped rolling over debt [fact-05].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 4 — 1 Million+ OTC Trades: Entangled across 8,000 counterparties with rehypothecated collateral triggering years of litigation [fact-05].

scenes.title: Business Snapshot 1.2: Systemic Risk & 4 Post-2008 OTC Reforms

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 1 — Systemic Domino Chain & SEFs: Stop Bank A from toppling Bank B and C by mandating electronic Swap Execution Facilities [fact-06].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 2 — Central Counterparties (CCPs): Interbank OTC trades clear through CCPs requiring initial and daily variation margins [fact-06].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 3 — Central Trade Repositories: All OTC transactions must be reported to central repositories for regulatory oversight [fact-06].
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Card 4 — Bilateral CSAs & Initial Margin: Non-cleared trades require Credit Support Annexes with daily variation and segregated initial margins [fact-06].

summarySteps: 1. Derivatives & Agricultural Hedging Origins: Derivatives derive value from underlying assets; locking in a September corn price protects both farmer and miller, standardized as a 5,000-bushel ($20,000) CME Corn contract [fact-01, fact-09].

2. Exchange-Traded Futures vs. OTC Forwards: Futures trade on public exchanges with standardized terms and daily clearing house margins; traditional forwards are customized bilateral contracts settled at maturity [fact-01, fact-02].

3. Global Derivatives Market Scale (BIS Dec 2014): The OTC market reaches $630 trillion in notional principal ($21 trillion gross market value), dwarfing the $65 trillion in exchange-traded underlying assets [fact-07].
4. Linear Terminal Payoff Equations: At maturity, a long forward or futures position yields Payoff = S_T - K, while a short position yields Payoff = K - S_T [fact-03].

5. Corporate FX Hedging with Bid/Offer Quotes: Using 3-month USD/GBP forwards (1.5736 Bid / 1.5742 Offer), ImportCo buys £10M at 1.5742 ($15,742,000 cost) and ExportCo sells £30M at 1.5736 ($47,208,000 revenue) [fact-08].

6. Leverage Ratio & Equity Wipeout Math: Equity capital percentage equals 1 / Leverage Ratio; at Lehman Brothers' 31:1 leverage in 2007, equity was just 3.23%, so a 3% to 4% asset drop wiped out 100% of equity [fact-04].

7. Lehman Brothers Bankruptcy (Sept 15, 2008): Driven by 31:1 leverage, aggressive risk culture (removing the CRO in 2007), unhedged subprime assets on short-term funding, and 1M+ OTC trades across 8,000 counterparties [fact-05].

8. Systemic Domino Risk & Post-2008 OTC Reforms: To stop Bank A's default from toppling Bank B and Bank C, regulators mandated SEFs, CCPs, Trade Repositories, and bilateral CSAs with segregated initial margin [fact-06].
bottomTakeaway: Futures and OTC forwards provide essential price-fixing tools across a $630+ trillion market, but surviving leverage and preventing systemic domino collapses require daily mark-to-market clearing, segregated collateral, and strict risk oversight [fact-02, fact-04, fact-05, fact-06, fact-07].
